handoff: Review #1 approves with no blocking findings: worktreesDir moved to <machine dir>/worktrees, AC1–AC10 each traced to a test, test and typecheck green. Minor: doctor's adoption advice now deletes worktrees; the orphan check could miss them under a symlinked home; the new integration file first runs in CI.

findings.title: Doctor's adoption advice now deletes the checkout's worktrees
findings.detail:
The orphaned-machine-dir advice is `rm -rf <mine> && mv <old> <mine>`. Since <mine>/worktrees now holds every live unit worktree, following it deletes uncommitted agent work. The spec puts doctor's adoption advice out of scope ('Out: … doctor's adoption advice'), so this is not blocking, but a person should know before shipping.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: A follow-up issue: have the advice move or keep worktrees/ (and run git worktree repair), or refuse while unit worktrees exist.

findings.title: The orphan check compares the paths as text, which a symlinked home could break
findings.detail:
The orphan check (and store/src/worktree.ts:91) matches `git worktree list` paths to `${worktreesDir(root)}/` with startsWith. The folder is now under the norn home instead of beside the repo. If a NORN_HOME_DIR or --home is reached through a symlink, and git records a resolved path (or the reverse), worktrees are no longer recognised. Unverified; the default ~/.norn is unaffected.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Normalise both sides with realpath before the comparison, or add a test with a symlinked home.

findings.title: The brief's part of AC6 is proven through the started receipt, not through what the brief shows
findings.detail:
AC6 says 'reads … the brief … then the path shown … is the worktree in the machine dir'. The test runs `brief` from the worktree and asserts that the started receipt's `worktree` is the machine-dir path, not a path in the brief's text. The brief does not appear to print the worktree path, so this is a reasonable proxy.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: None needed, unless the brief should print the path; QA can confirm.
